extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and attorneys subject to USPTO discipline
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order resolving a disciplinary complaint against a USPTO-registered patent attorney by stipulation and settlement, setting forth findings, legal conclusions, sanctions, reporting obligations, publication/notice requirements, and procedures if probation is violated.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction and authority to approve settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter and the authority to approve the Proposed Settlement Agreement pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may resolve disciplinary actions by settlement that satisfy 37 C.F.R. § 11.26; the Director's statutory/regulatory authority provides the basis for approving stipulated dispositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation based on state suspension (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges that his conduct violated the Disciplinary Rules of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility, specifically 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a) and (b) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5), by being suspended from practice as an attorney on ethical grounds by any duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A suspension from practice by a state on ethical grounds constitutes a basis for discipline under the USPTO rules referenced; such a suspension may be treated as the predicate violation in USPTO proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive misconduct findings (dishonesty/fraud/misrepresentation/false evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Texas State Bar found that Respondent knowingly offered or used evidence that Respondent knew to be false and that Respondent engaged in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct involving knowingly offering/using false evidence or other dishonesty/fraud/deceit/misrepresentation is an aggravating ethical violation supporting suspension and other discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreed sanction: stayed suspension plus probation
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) Respondent be suspended for a period of twenty-four (24) months ... (ii) the suspension be immediately stayed ...; Respondent shall serve a twenty-four month probationary period commencing on the date the Final Order is signed; Respondent shall be permitted to practice ... during his probationary period unless the stay ... is lifted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A stayed suspension coupled with probation is an available disposition; the stay allows continued practice during probation unless lifted for violations. The Final Order specifies duration and immediate effect terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions of state probation and related obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Texas State Bar suspended Respondent for two (2) years, with the suspension fully probated, provided that (i) Respondent does not violate any term of the judgment, (ii) Respondent not engage in professional misconduct, (iii) Respondent not violate any state or federal criminal statutes, (iv) Respondent keep the State Bar of Texas informed of his current address, (v) Respondent comply with Minimum Continuing Legal Education requirements for the state of Texas, (vi) Respondent comply with Texas State IOLTA requirements, (vii) Respondent promptly respond to any request for information from the Texas State Bar, (viii) Respondent pay attorney's fees to the Texas State Bar, and (ix) Respondent complete ... six additional hours of Ethics CLE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terms imposed by a state disciplinary body (CLE, reporting, IOLTA, fees, etc.) may be incorporated as facts supporting USPTO action and signal compliance expectations while on probation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirement for revocation of state probation (37 C.F.R. § 10.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 10.24, report in writing any revocation of his probation in Texas to the OED Director within thirty days of the revocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered practitioners must timely notify OED of any revocation of state-imposed probation within 30 days; failure to report may trigger further disciplinary steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED procedure on suspected probation violation (Order to Show Cause and response period)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director is of the opinion that Respondent, during the probationary period, failed to comply with any provision of the Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule, the OED Director shall: (A) issue to Respondent an Order to Show Cause why the USPTO Director ... should not order that the stay ... be lifted and Respondent be immediately suspended ...; (B) send the Order to Show Cause to Respondent at the last address of record ...; and (C) grant Respondent fifteen (15) days to respond to the Order to Show Cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED follows a notice-and-response procedure (Order to Show Cause, service to address of record, 15-day response window) before requesting lifting of a stayed suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to USPTO Director and request to lift stay after OED determination
rubrics_metrics.description: After the 15-day response period, if the OED Director remains of the opinion that Respondent failed to comply, the OED Director shall deliver to the USPTO Director: (i) the Order to Show Cause, (ii) Respondent's response, if any, and (iii) evidence causing the OED Director to be of the opinion ... and request that the USPTO Director ... immediately lift the stay of the suspension and suspend Respondent for up to twenty-four (24) months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED compiles the record and formally requests the Director lift the stay and impose the stayed suspension; this is the pathway from probation noncompliance to immediate suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences upon lifting stay and actual suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent is suspended pursuant to these provisions: (1) Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; (2) the OED Director shall disseminate information in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59; (3) the USPTO shall promptly dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO customer numbers and Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) certificates; (4) Respondent shall not use any USPTO customer number or PKI certificate unless and until he is reinstated; and (5) Respondent may not obtain a USPTO customer number or a PKI certificate unless and until he is reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actual suspension triggers regulatory compliance (§11.58), public dissemination (§11.59), and technical/account actions (dissociation and blocking of customer numbers/PKI certificates) preventing practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of review on immediate suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event that the USPTO Director or his designee lifts the stay ... and Respondent seeks a review of the USPTO Director's decision ... any such review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the immediate suspension of Respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An appeal or request for review does not stay the immediate effect of a Director's lifting of a stayed suspension; suspension is effective notwithstanding review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-exclusivity of settlement as bar to further discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Proposed Settlement Agreement or the Final Order shall prevent the Office from seeking discipline against Respondent in accordance with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.34 through 11.57 for the misconduct that caused the stay of the suspension to be lifted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement does not immunize a practitioner from additional disciplinary proceedings for the same misconduct if conditions are violated; the Office retains authority to pursue further discipline under the cited rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice obligations (OED Reading Room, Official Gazette, and notice to agencies/courts/public)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room electronically; the OED Director shall publish the following Notice of Stayed Suspension in the Official Gazette ... Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public disclosure of discipline (Reading Room, Official Gazette) and notice to relevant state agencies and courts is required by regulation and is part of remedial/transparent enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of this record in future disciplinary matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, be considered (i) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct brought to the attention of the Office, and/or (ii) in any future disciplinary proceeding (1) as an aggravating factor to be taken into consideration in determining any discipline to be imposed and/or (2) to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior disciplinary records are admissible and may be used both to aggravate sanctions and to rebut future representations in later proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement specified that each party bears its own costs rather than awarding costs against the respondent or OED.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition for not serving stayed suspension (time-limited stay)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the stay of the suspension ... is not lifted by order of the USPTO Director or his designee by the end of the probationary period, Respondent is not required to serve the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A stayed suspension will not be converted into an active suspension if the Director does not lift the stay by the end of probation; this sets a firm end-point for the conditional discipline.
